numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When the power equation has no solution and the root finder fails to converge, solve_power still returns `val`, described as the last solver-evaluated point (typically a bracket bound such as `array([10.])`), even though a `ConvergenceWarning` is emitted. After the fix, the function sets `val = np.nan` when `success != 1`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Return `nan` (`np.nan`) in cases where the root finder fails to converge (`success != 1`), so a caller does not treat the last evaluated bracket bound as a valid sample size. Convergence cases should not change.
trigger_conditions: A one-sided test is requested where the `effect_size` points into the wrong tail (no `nobs` reaches the target power).
The underlying root-finding for `Power.solve_power` does not converge (root finder emits a `ConvergenceWarning`; `success` is set to 0).

input_output_examples.source: PR#9884 problem statement shows the call and that the previous behavior returns `array([10.])` after a `ConvergenceWarning`; the fix description specifies returning `np.nan` when `success != 1`.

oracle_clues: A `ConvergenceWarning` is emitted when there is no solution; previously, solve_power returned the last evaluated root-finder point (often a bracket bound like `10`).
The fix is explicitly keyed off the existing `success` flag: when `success != 1`, set `val = np.nan` before returning.
The regression test asserts that the sign-mismatched one-sided cases return `nan` and that a solvable control case still returns a finite value.
